title: Regular-module scalar comparison in a monoidal coefficient diagram
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be braided monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category, det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport]. Assume that $\mathcal E$ has coequalizers and that tensoring on either side preserves colimits. Let $P:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$ and $F:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ be strong monoidal functors [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor], with unit comparisons $\varepsilon_P,\varepsilon_Q,\varepsilon_F$. Supply a monoidal natural isomorphism $c:F\circ P\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$, meaning a natural isomorphism compatible with the unit and tensor comparisons. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring object [sk-def-sfb-ring-object]. Give $R=P\Lambda$, $T=F(R)$ and $S=Q\Lambda$ their transported ring structures [def-sfb-modobj-transport], and assume that $R,T,S$ are commutative. Put $\alpha=c_\Lambda:T\xrightarrow{\sim}S$, a ring isomorphism, and $H=\operatorname{Ext}_\alpha\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(F):\operatorname{Mod}_R(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Mod}_S(\mathcal E)$ [def-sfb-modobj-extension, sk-def-sfb-module-objects].
For every $a:\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}\to\Lambda$, put $a_R=P(a)\varepsilon_P$ and $a_S=Q(a)\varepsilon_Q$. For a ring object $Z$ and $b:\mathbf1\to Z$, write $t_b=\mu_Z\circ(b\otimes1_Z)\circ\lambda_Z^{-1}:Z\to Z$, where $\lambda$ is the left unitor. These multiplication maps are endomorphisms of the corresponding regular modules when $Z$ is commutative.
Then $P(t_a)=t_{a_R}$, $Q(t_a)=t_{a_S}$ and $\alpha\circ F(t_{a_R})=t_{a_S}\circ\alpha$. Transport identifies $\operatorname{mapMod}(F)(R)$ with the regular $T$-module by the identity on the underlying object. There is a canonical $S$-module isomorphism $e:H(R)\xrightarrow{\sim}S$. Under $H(R)=S\otimes_T T$, with balancing coequalizer map $q:S\otimes T\to S\otimes_T T$, it is specified by
$$e\circ q=\mu_S\circ(1_S\otimes\alpha),\qquad e^{-1}=q\circ(1_S\otimes\eta_T)\circ\rho_S^{-1},$$
where $\eta_T$ is the ring unit and $\rho_S$ the ambient right unitor. For every $a$ as above, this same isomorphism satisfies
$$e\circ H(t_{a_R})=t_{a_S}\circ e.$$
All equalities involving $q$ are equalities of morphisms in $\mathcal E$, without an assumption that sections of a sheafified tensor product are pure tensors.
